title: Vysaeth
dek: A king found in his silent underground city, whose journal explains why he chose lichdom to guard his people’s treasures.

facts.Purpose: Preservation of his people’s legacy · his journal account
facts.Last observed: Immobile in the tomb; Quake places his skeletal remains in lava · 7 Jul 2024
facts.Ultimate fate: Not established by disposal of the remains

body:
In the journal recovered from his tomb, Vysaeth describes becoming a lich to protect his realm’s treasures, knowledge and legacy. He presents the transformation as a sacrifice made under threat. That is his account of his purpose, not an independent verdict that every action served only preservation.

The company that finds him on 7 Jul 2024 reaches a city still working around an almost motionless king. Forges run on volcanic heat, unfinished weapons lie in the streets, and the dead gather around five thrones. Saray reads the journal beside his body while Elenia tries to speak to him.

The city beneath the last statue

The expedition begins among the towering statues outside the Tower of Gael. Quake reads their order as a succession of rulers, with the newer monuments farther from the tower. The earliest carvings show gardens and pavilions; later monuments carry increasingly violent histories. The last warrior statue stands beyond the ruined city, with a sealed tomb at its foot and an unnatural storm around it.

Dale reads the old Elvish inscription. The travelers combine their magic to open the entrance, and the chambers below reveal an underground city built around a vast forge. Machinery continues to turn on lava power. Half-finished swords and larger engines of war remain among the forges. The streets show no struggle and no food; the travelers have reached a preserved workshop whose workers are gone.

At the center, a bridge leads over lava to five thrones. One complete skeletal figure remains amid artifacts and valuable spell components. Bones lie around it, many already pushed into the molten rock. The king’s treasures have survived more visibly than his people.

A brother’s account of Roderick

His journal calls Roderick ambitious, greedy, insidious, and destructive. Some or all of that may be true, but the Codex preserves the speaker: this is Endora’s brother describing the man who tried to reclaim her and threatened his realm.

Vysaeth’s first entry places the decision after his sister’s illness and death. He describes Duke Roderick seizing power, trying to call her soul back and threatening the treasures accumulated by the kingdom. To Vysaeth, those objects hold the history and pride of his people. He fears losing the things he has been charged to protect.

He writes that he turned to forbidden necromancy and bound himself into undeath so he would have time to fortify the sanctuary. The account contains grief, fear of plunder and a ruler’s defense of his own conduct. Roderick’s ambitions reach the travelers through a man who believed they justified turning himself into a lich.

Two answers to loss

Vysaeth and Roderick both violate nature after losing Endora. Vysaeth tries to preserve a people and their history; Roderick tries to restore a person. Both refuse disappearance. Both pay horrifying prices.

Vysaeth’s middle entry describes the work of adding ward after ward around the underground city. In the final entry, he says at least a century has passed since his transformation. Ancient spells and his people’s life force have sustained his powers, but that strength is fading and his last subjects have long since died. He prepares to seal the entrances and remain alone with what they left behind.

His words claim an endurance that outlasts the community it was meant to serve. The travelers can see the immaculate machinery and the bones. They cannot recover every death, decision or year between the retreat underground and the journal’s final entry.

The guardian who cannot answer

When Saray examines the skeleton, the narrator describes a being still conscious of the company but unable to move or speak, channeling the magic that protects the place. Elenia approaches peacefully and tries to communicate. The king gives no answer; what remains of him functions as a magical conduit.

Elenia also tries to call a voice from another skull. There is no soul to answer, and the narration extends that absence to the bones around them. Her suspicion that the magic has been feeding on souls remains her explanation. The scene does not establish that Vysaeth deliberately killed his subjects or supply a complete account of what happened to them.

Saray worries that touching the treasure will trigger a trap. Her examination finds no warding magic in that chamber: the company has already proved itself by entering. The surviving artifacts are useful, but the guardian is in no condition to negotiate their removal.

Quake’s promise and the broken entrance

A shadow has already disturbed the dust and escapes with a mighty sword. Elenia and Saray notice it, but it moves through walls and outruns their pursuit. As Quake gathers the remaining items, another shadow demon opens the door from inside.

Quake addresses the king before leaving: “King Vysaeth, I will watch over and guard your kingdom's Legacy.” He salutes, gently lifts the skeleton and places it in the lava. His promise passes the keeping of the recovered objects to a living traveler; the scene does not establish the lich’s ultimate fate.

A death dragon appears afterward, kills Dale and breaks the entrance as it flies into the wasteland. On the way back, Wrath thanks the survivors for finishing his beloved’s brother and speaks of the sword. His greeting joins the family history in the journal to an enemy now standing before them.

The checked account does not identify the escaping sword-bearer or establish that putting Vysaeth’s remains in the lava caused the dragon’s arrival. The journal and the company’s discoveries survive as distinct accounts of a ruler whose attempt to protect a people ends in an empty city.

Continue reading Gael · Roderick / Wrath · Quake · Saray · Elenia · Dale

evidence.label: Observed quest scene
evidence.summary: Narration establishes the scene and actions; statements and motives retain their speakers.

evidence.label: Attributed journal account
evidence.summary: The narrator presents written journal entries. Vysaeth’s judgments about Roderick and his own motives remain interested testimony; this is not an impartial history of the succession.

evidence.label: Witnessed quest scenes & attributed accounts
evidence.summary: Vysaeth’s duration, intent and account of his people come from his journal; the surviving city and bones are witnessed separately. No exact ancient date or full casualty history is assigned.

evidence.label: Witnessed quest scenes & attributed accounts
evidence.summary: The narrator establishes the immobile conduit and failed attempt to call a soul. Elenia’s proposed explanation and Saray’s initial fear remain attributed; no universal lich mechanism is inferred.

sections.title: Quake’s promise and the broken entrance

evidence.label: Witnessed quest scenes & attributed accounts
evidence.summary: The order of removal, apparition and attack is witnessed; causation and the thief’s identity remain unproved. Wrath’s thanks are his words. Disposal of remains does not establish irreversible destruction of a lich.
